title: A Kid Asks the TV a Question, Gets Back a Real Explainer | vitalii.no
description:
When one of my kids asked why the moon has phases, or what a parabola is, there was no good way to answer at their level. A text reply doesn't stick, and generic YouTube explainers are either pitched wrong for a six-year-old's vocabulary or don't match the specific question asked, in Ukrainian and Norwegian both.

I built a dedicated video engine for the kiosk's new explain button. A child asks a question by voice or text to a private bot, the words get turned into a timed scene plan, and that plan drives camera flights over named places, 3D models, small math animations and animated emoji actors, narrated with a generated voice, rendered with Remotion. Rendering happens off-device, split into chunks that finish together, because the kiosk itself has no spare GPU.

The first full plan, 'chicken or egg', rendered end to end, with the render job splitting into up to six parallel chunks per video and the kiosk's status row now showing a live state for every question asked.
